2. Load the data and perform the analysis needed to answer each question rigorously (check assumptions, report exact statistics).
3. When confident, call submit_answer with one answer per question. Answer concisely — a number, short phrase, or sentence as the question demands. Do not refuse unless the data genuinely cannot answer the question.

You may take multiple steps. Use your budget wisely.

Study: bix-10


Questions to answer:
- [bix-10-q1] What is the odds ratio of higher COVID-19 severity (encoded in the column AESEV) associated with BCG vaccination in a multivariable ordinal logistic regression model that includes patient interaction frequency variables as covariates?
- [bix-10-q2] Using an ordinal logistic regression model (ordered logit), what is the odds ratio associated with healthcare workers' expected patient interaction (expect_interact_cat) on the likelihood of reporting higher COVID-19 severity (AESEV), after adjusting for number of patients seen (patients_seen_cat) and BCG vaccination status (TRTGRP_cat)?
- [bix-10-q3] In which patient volume group (number of patients seen) do healthcare workers show statistically significant differences (p<0.05) in COVID-19 severity between BCG vaccination and placebo groups based on chi-square analysis?
- [bix-10-q4] Using a chi-square test, what is the p-value for the association between BCG vaccination and COVID-19 severity among healthcare workers who expect to interact with patients?
- [bix-10-q5] For healthcare workers seeing over 100 patients, what is the statistical significance (p-value) of the association between vaccination status and disease severity?
- [bix-10-q6] When performing a Chi-square test of independence to examine the association between BCG vaccination status (BCG vs Placebo) and COVID-19 disease severity among healthcare workers who see 1-50 patients, what is the p-value of the statistical test?
- [bix-10-q7] What is the percentage reduction in odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity among healthcare workers expected to interact with patients versus those who do not, when controlling for BCG vaccination and number of patients seen?

When you have answered all questions, call submit_answer with a JSON object mapping each question id to your answer.

import pandas as pd, os
from statsmodels.miscmodels.ordinal_model import OrderedModel

DATA_DIR = os.environ['DATA_DIR']

ae = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'TASK008_BCG-CORONA_AE.csv'), encoding='latin1')
dm = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'TASK008_BCG-CORONA_DM.csv'), encoding='latin1')

covid = ae[ae['AEPT']=='COVID-19'].copy()
covid = covid.groupby('USUBJID', as_index=False)['AESEV'].max()

covid_dm = covid.merge(dm[['USUBJID','TRTGRP','patients_seen','expect_interact']], on='USUBJID', how='left')

covid_dm = covid_dm.dropna(subset=['AESEV'])

# encode
covid_dm['TRTGRP_cat'] = covid_dm['TRTGRP'].map({'BCG':1,'Placebo':0})

# ordered patients_seen
order = ['1-50','51-100','>100']
cat_type = pd.CategoricalDtype(categories=order, ordered=True)
covid_dm['patients_seen_cat'] = covid_dm['patients_seen'].astype('category').cat.set_categories(order, ordered=True)

covid_dm['expect_interact_cat'] = covid_dm['expect_interact'].map({'Yes':1,'No':0})

covid_dm = covid_dm.dropna(subset=['TRTGRP_cat','patients_seen_cat','expect_interact_cat'])

covid_dm['AESEV_int'] = covid_dm['AESEV'].astype(int)

print(covid_dm[['AESEV_int','TRTGRP_cat','patients_seen_cat','expect_interact_cat']].head())
print(covid_dm['patients_seen_cat'].value_counts())

# design matrix
X = pd.get_dummies(covid_dm[['TRTGRP_cat','patients_seen_cat','expect_interact_cat']], drop_first=False)
print(X.head())

mod = OrderedModel(covid_dm['AESEV_int'], X, distr='logit')
res = mod.fit(method='bfgs', disp=False)
print(res.summary())

import numpy as np

or_bcg = np.exp(params['TRTGRP_cat']) if 'TRTGRP_cat' in params else None
